title: Studio authoring — the admin/maker loop: packages, objects, views, record pages, draft→publish

items.title: The first-run authoring loop closes: package → object → record → app → publish → end-user, zero code, zero restarts
personas: end user (same account driving the published app)

requires: a fresh boot of the showcase example — objectstack dev --ui --seed-admin -p <port> -d file:/tmp/<run>/data.db (the audit's environment: a console built from this tree with `pnpm console:build`, seeded admin admin@objectos.ai/admin123)
knownGaps: SUPERSEDED (QA run #24571): publish is no longer one click with no confirmation. Publish opens the 'Pending changes' review sheet — every pending draft listed as New or Update, each expanding into the keys it changes, and a separate 'Publish all' confirm (objectui app-shell preview/DraftChangesPanel.tsx, mounted by StudioDesignSurface.tsx; the audit's finding 3 / ADR-0016 §3.6 step 4). A review step now exists; do not score its presence or absence here — this item scores the loop

SUPERSEDED (QA run #21056): a new app no longer scaffolds zero nav items — the Create-app dialog seeds the app's navigation from the package's objects behind a checkbox that defaults ON (objectui StudioDesignSurface appAddObjects, objectui#2262). With it on, step 5's nav item already exists and the Interfaces step confirms it rather than builds it; only with it unticked does the manual wiring remain the contract. Do not expect zero items
mixed-language Studio chrome (audit finding 4) is asserted by i18n.studio-follows-app-locale — locale consistency is that item's business, not this one's

steps: boot the showcase example (objectstack dev --ui --seed-admin -p <port> -d file:/tmp/<run>/data.db), sign in as admin@objectos.ai/admin123, and note the boot timestamp in the server log (the zero-restart clause reads it later)

Home → the build chip → create a NEW writable package (维修中心 / com.example.repairs, namespace repairs) via the new-package wizard. Type the identifier yourself: a CJK-only display name derives no package id (objectui PackageFormDialog.tsx toIdSegment: 'Empty when nothing usable remains (a CJK-only name, say)'), and the namespace derives from the id you type. The build chip has two forms (ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/home/HomePage.tsx): with an agent catalog it reads 'Build an app' (data-testid home-build-app) and opens the Studio landing, where New package opens the wizard; with none it reads 'New in Studio' (home-build-in-studio) and opens Studio with the New package dialog already open, the form QA run #27481 met on the stock showcase. Record which

Data pillar → new object 'Repair Ticket' (the identifier auto-suggests repair_ticket from the display name, and the dialog PREFIXES it with the package namespace, so the object is named repairs_repair_ticket — the name every later step and clause uses (framework#2694, objectui StudioDesignSurface prefixObjectName). The dialog also carries an OWD (sharing model) choice, pre-selected to the platform's recommended baseline: confirm or change it, then click 'Save as draft', the dialog's confirm button (engine.studio.createDraft; no Studio create dialog has a button named Create)) → add a picklist field Status with 3 values. There is no Save draft button: the designer autosaves, and a picklist field is held unsaved until it has at least one option (the status line reads 'Not saved yet: the field “Status” needs at least one option'), so add the field and fill its options, and the draft save fires

open the Changes panel and Publish, then confirm with 'Publish all' in the review sheet; the toast names the count — 'Published 1 item in this package (one atomic release)' (objectui#11807; 'Published all drafts in this package' is the fallback when the count is unknown)
create a record in the runtime-faithful Records grid with a Status value chosen
Create app 'Repair Center' (identifier auto-suggested) → Interfaces pillar → add a nav item bound to repairs_repair_ticket → Publish

return to the console Home (/_console/home — the Studio header's house icon goes to the Studio landing, 'Studio home', and from the landing the console Home is its top bar's product mark, the link named 'PRODUCT home' (e.g. 'ObjectOS home'; data-testid app-bar-product-home, ui/packages/app-shell/src/layout/AppHeader.tsx ProductHomeMark), which goes to the deployment's home path, /_console/home on stock; no control on that bar is named plain 'Home'): the launcher must show Repair Center; open it and drive the end-user list

verify server truth after each publish: GET /api/v1/meta/object/repairs_repair_ticket, GET /api/v1/data/repairs_repair_ticket, GET /api/v1/meta/app?id=<the new app NAME, e.g. repair_center> — ?id= matches the App document name, NOT the package id com.example.repairs; fetch /api/v1/meta/app with no query first to read the name the wizard actually minted

negative probe: on the READ-ONLY com.example.showcase package there is no gesture to drive — the console HIDES New object and Add field there (objectui StudioDesignSurface gates them on !readOnly) — so the probe is a FORGED request: send the authoring write the gesture would have made straight to the metadata write door against that package, and capture the server response (QA run #21056 read 422 WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED and 403 ITEM_LOCKED)

acceptance.clause: package create round-trips and the package switcher lists the new writable package without a page reload
acceptance.verify: the create POST succeeds and the switcher shows the package in the same session. ui/e2e/live/studio-object-designer.spec.ts test F1 pins it (read in objectui at cf153eb2e535, blob 58a7f1cbf024, before the import under ui/): it creates a package through the switcher's New package dialog by the testids studio-pkg-chip, package-form-id-input and package-form-submit, all declared in ui/packages/app-shell (StudioDesignSurface.tsx, PackageFormDialog.tsx), and asserts that the surface moved into the new package and that the switcher lists it by name with no reload. Run F1 from ui/ with `pnpm test:e2e:live studio-object-designer.spec.ts` against a live boot (RUNNER, the objectui-pinned-automation fact) and cite its output naming the commit, or drive the clause by hand. Note the new-package wizard's own state, objectui#11327

acceptance.clause: the published object is server-real: the meta read returns repairs_repair_ticket with the authored picklist field carrying exactly the 3 authored options — never ticked off the designer repaint
acceptance.verify: GET /api/v1/meta/object/repairs_repair_ticket body contains the Status field with its 3 options

acceptance.clause: the record entered in the Studio Records grid persists to the data plane
acceptance.verify: GET /api/v1/data/repairs_repair_ticket lists the record with the chosen Status value stored under the field's API name

acceptance.clause: the published app is live in the Home launcher and the end-user list renders the record with the picklist LABEL chip (label resolution, not the raw value)
acceptance.verify: launcher screenshot shows Repair Center; end-user list screenshot shows the record row with the label chip; GET /api/v1/meta/app?id=<the new app NAME> carries the nav item bound to the object
acceptance.evidence: the two screenshots + the app meta read

acceptance.clause: the loop closes with ZERO server restarts and zero code — publish alone made the package, object, and app live (the audit's benchmark: 'Zero code, no dead ends, minutes end-to-end')
acceptance.verify: the server log shows a single boot for the whole loop; no restart was performed between the first step and the end-user list
acceptance.evidence: server log excerpt spanning the run

acceptance.clause: the writable/read-only gate is enforced SERVER-side: the authoring write into com.example.showcase is rejected by the server even where the client lets the gesture through
acceptance.verify: the negative probe's server response is a rejection naming the read-only/installed-package cause (audit finding 1 proved this side holds); the client-side lock itself is access-security.readonly-package-locks-studio — cite a pass there, do not re-prove the DOM lock here

negative: silent acceptance of an authoring write into a read-only package is a FAIL (ADR-0124 D1 — the server is the authoritative gate; the client lock is courtesy)
a 'published' app absent from the Home launcher, or an end-user list rendering raw picklist values instead of labels, is a FAIL

requires: a writable package to author into (create one via the Studio wizard or POST /api/v1/packages — the source-loaded com.example.showcase is read-only and rejects designer saves server-side)
knownGaps: AUTOMATION LIVES UNDER ui/ — `automated.ref` names objectui specs, and since objectui was imported into this repository they resolve at ui/PATH in this checkout. A jsdom unit pin runs here (`pnpm --filter @object-ui/PKG exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 FILE`); a ui/e2e/live spec runs from ui/ with `pnpm test:e2e:live SPEC` against a live backend and the console dev server (the prerequisites are in ui/playwright.live.config.ts). Cite the output naming the commit, or drive the item by hand in the browser and score it as a manual run. ⛔ Never score it as covered on the strength of the `automated` field alone — an unrun pin is a claim, not evidence. Full protocol: RUNNER.md, the objectui-pinned-automation standing fact.

steps: open Studio on the writable package — /_console/studio/PKG/data (PKG = the writable package's id; note its namespace NS, from GET /api/v1/packages) — and click New object. Studio is the authoring door this item drives (QA run #26715 drove every clause through it); the Setup metadata editor (/_console/apps/setup/metadata/object/new?package=PKG) is a second door onto the same save, and it is the one the objectui pins in automated.ref drive. ⛔ Not /_console/apps/com.objectstack.studio/…: the studio app is not loaded on a stock boot (RUNNER.md environment facts), so that route renders inside another app's chrome

in the New object dialog type the Label 'Repair Asset', THEN type the identifier repair_asset character by character (never .fill — the F2 per-keystroke-sanitisation bug only reproduces when typed) and confirm its underscore survives. The dialog applies the package namespace itself: it previews and stores NS_repair_asset (StudioDesignSurface prefixObjectName, objectui CreateItemDialog.storedName-11792 — no double prefix when NS_ is typed as well), which the publish gate requires in a namespaced package (NAMESPACE_PREFIX). Type the identifier after the Label, and re-check it before 'Save as draft' (objectui#12680: a Label typed after a hand-typed identifier can re-derive it). Keep the pre-selected OWD choice and click 'Save as draft' (the dialog's confirm button, engine.studio.createDraft; no Studio create dialog has a button named Create)
add a Text field, set its label to 'Asset Code', blur — the API name input must derive asset_code (F3)

add a Picklist field and author its 3 real options, THEN add one EMPTY option row; wait out the debounced live validation — no validation banner may appear for the empty row (F4). ⚠ Order matters: with NO real option yet the select-needs-options banner fires, legitimately — the empty rows ARE dropped, so the field has no options — which collides with a literal 'no banner' (objectui F4, as repaired at 0b36ffa, gives its picklist one real option first for this reason). Assert the empty-row half with real options present

let the autosave land (Studio has no Save button: the status line reads 'Saved HH:MM'), then Publish → the review sheet → 'Publish all'; GET /api/v1/meta/object/NS_repair_asset and record the full field list and its order

reopen the object in the Data pillar: rename one picklist value, then reorder the fields on the Form tab — the form designer is dnd-kit (ObjectFormDesigner.tsx: a PointerSensor with a 4 px activation distance and a KeyboardSensor), so drag with intermediate pointer moves past 4 px, or focus a field's drag handle and press Space, an arrow key, Space; a single synthetic jump does not start a drag (automation-input). Let the autosave land and Publish again
GET /api/v1/meta/object/NS_repair_asset again — the rename AND the new field order must be in the persisted metadata, not just the canvas
create a record via the Records tab and GET /api/v1/data/NS_repair_asset/<id> — the stored column key must be the derived API name (asset_code)

items.title: List + form view authoring goes live in the running app on publish — no server restart
personas: end user (consumes the published views). A runtime-authored object grants no non-admin persona any access, so a non-admin list render needs a permission-set grant on it first; without one, score the end-user surfaces as the admin and say so (QA run #24571)

requires: a runtime-authored object in a writable package to bind views to (e.g. repair_asset from studio-authoring.object-designer-roundtrip), so no shipped showcase view is mutated. The object must declare a `sharingModel`, one of private, public_read, public_read_write or controlled_by_parent (packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts; controlled_by_parent also needs a master_detail parent; any other value, such as read_write, answers 422, QA run #27441): its draft PUT answers 200 without one, but publish refuses it (security-owd-unset, error tier — packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts), so an object authored without it never goes live (QA run #24571)

the object must hold NO stored view container yet — a fresh scratch object is safest. A second container whose expansion serves names an existing container already serves (OBJECT.default / OBJECT.form) is refused 400 VALIDATION_ERROR naming the other owner (packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, viewContainerNameCollisionRefusal), and that refusal reads like a failed draft door (QA run #26715 met it). If the object already has one, edit that container (add the views as its members) rather than authoring a second

steps: author a view CONTAINER draft via the metadata draft door: PUT /api/v1/meta/view/qa_repair_asset_views?mode=draft with { object: 'repair_asset', list: { type: 'grid', columns: [...] }, form: { ... } } — the container's own keys are list/form/listViews/formViews (ViewSchema); capture the receipt. A 400 VALIDATION_ERROR naming another container as the owner of the names is the second-container collision (fixtures.requires[1]), not this item's FAIL: re-run on an object with no stored container
as an end user, open the object's list BEFORE publishing: it must still render the previously published views (or the synthesized default) — the draft is staged only

items.title: Metadata draft→publish lifecycle: drafts staged not served, publish flips visibility atomically, conflicts and invalid drafts refused, and the history/audit/diff/rollback forensics tell the truth

requires: scratch metadata names only (e.g. qa_lifecycle_probe) via the draft door PUT /api/v1/meta/<type>/<name>?mode=draft — no shipped showcase file is touched
a writable package with two stageable drafts for the package-wide publish-drafts door
knownGaps: NO PIN COVERS A FULL CLAUSE — `automated` was dropped at revision 8, so this P1 item is hand-driven (Tier 2). packages/qa/dogfood/test/dashboard-designer-roundtrip.dogfood.test.ts, the pin it cited, saves a layout-less dashboard as a draft (PUT ?mode=draft answers 200), publishes it (200) and reads it back as { type, name, item } with its three widgets. That is acceptance[1]'s post-publish half and nothing more: it asserts no state:'draft' receipt and makes no pre-publish read (acceptance[0], and acceptance[1]'s never-served half), and it probes none of acceptance[2]–[11]: no second draft, stale If-Match, publish-drafts batch, invalid draft, Studio chrome, history, diff, rollback, audit or X-Actor. So it scores no clause (Tier 1 run #24598: every clause not-run). Re-add `automated` only with a pin that asserts a full clause.

steps: author a dashboard draft: PUT /api/v1/meta/dashboard/qa_lifecycle_probe?mode=draft with one dataset-bound widget (dataset: showcase_task_metrics, dimensions: ['status'], values: ['task_count']) — the same door areas/dashboards.json exercises
record the receipt: { success, version, seq, state: 'draft' }

BOTH sides pre-publish: GET /api/v1/meta/dashboard/qa_lifecycle_probe as the runtime read → 404 (never published) — the draft body must not be served; in Studio the item header shows the draft line 'Draft · N unpublished' (objectui#12725, studioItemDraftStatus.ts; N is the package's pending count) and a numbered pill on the Changes button (objectui#12459). For the Studio half stage the draft in a WRITABLE package (?package=PKG on the draft PUT): the pill counts the pending drafts of the package in scope, and an env-wide, package-less draft is counted in no package scope, so it shows no pill. Open the item in Studio through that package: stage, in the same package, an app draft whose navigation names the dashboard (e.g. an entry of type dashboard, dashboardName qa_lifecycle_probe) and select that entry in the Interfaces pillar — a package with no app shows 'This package has no app yet' and no dashboard to select, so no chip can render; the pill then counts both drafts
publish per-ref: POST /api/v1/meta/dashboard/qa_lifecycle_probe/publish → 200; GET now serves the authored body
author a SECOND draft revision on the same name and confirm the live read keeps serving revision 1 until that draft is published
concurrency guard: re-PUT with the STALE version as If-Match and capture the 409

package-wide door: stage two drafts in the writable package and POST /api/v1/packages/<pkg id>/publish-drafts — both flip in one atomic release (the audit's 'Published all drafts in this package (one atomic release)' toast); capture the STATUS and the BODY separately, because the abort path answers 200 with data.success:false (see the clause below)
author an INVALID draft (a widget carrying a stray legacy key) and attempt its publish — the author-time gate must reject the draft→active transition (#4463)

meta forensics (after the two publishes of qa_lifecycle_probe — revision 1, then the second revision): GET /api/v1/meta/dashboard/qa_lifecycle_probe/history — the durable sys_metadata_history events must list BOTH published revisions (a dashboard is an overlay type, so history is real; a non-overlay type answers { events: [] } by design). History counts draft saves AND publishes, so two save-draft-then-publish rounds read v1 (draft), v2 (its publish), v3 (draft), v4 (publish): read the two PUBLISH versions off this body for the diff step, steps[9] (QA run #23166 read v2 and v4)

GET /api/v1/meta/dashboard/qa_lifecycle_probe/diff?from=<first publish version>&to=<second publish version> — the two publish versions read off /history in steps[8] (v2 and v4 on a clean two-round run; QA run #26715 read v2 and v5, because one extra If-Match draft save sat between them); the diff is SHALLOW by design — it names the changed TOP-LEVEL key (`widgets`, with its whole before/after value) and only the keys that differ, never the whole body and never a path inside the array (packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts#diffShallow: deep structural diffs are out of scope, Studio renders the full bodies side by side). ⛔ Not ?from=1&to=2: v1 → v2 is a draft save and its own publish, which differ in nothing (changed []), and a default previous-vs-current read can land on the same draft/publish pair

POST /api/v1/meta/dashboard/qa_lifecycle_probe/rollback with { toVersion: 1 }, driven under an authenticated session so the actor is attributable — the authenticated identity is the ONLY source ([#7941]; resolveMetaWriteActor no longer consults `X-Actor` at all); the runtime GET must then serve revision 1's body again and the rendered dashboard must show revision 1's widget

repeat the rollback (or another /meta write on this item, e.g. a follow-up draft save) while ALSO sending header `X-Actor: someone_else_entirely` on the authenticated request — the header must NOT change the recorded actor: the audit/history rows for that action still name the authenticated runner's own identity, never `someone_else_entirely` ([#7941] — pinned at the unit layer in packages/rest/src/meta-write-actor-identity.test.ts)
attempt a rollback with a missing/invalid toVersion and capture the 400 INVALID_REQUEST guard

GET /api/v1/meta/dashboard/qa_lifecycle_probe/audit — the save/publish/rollback rows must carry the acting user; run every forensics probe against the REST route-manager server os dev serves, NEVER a simulated dispatch (the dispatcher /meta branch swallows /history as a compound name and 404s)

acceptance.clause: a draft save answers state:'draft' and is staged only — the runtime read does not serve it (both sides captured: receipt + 404/last-active read)
acceptance.verify: PUT receipt has state:'draft' (SaveMetaItemResponseSchema); the follow-up GET returns 404 (or the last ACTIVE body for a previously-published name), never the draft body

acceptance.clause: publish flips visibility exactly once: the post-publish read serves the authored body; the pre-publish read never did
acceptance.verify: POST /meta/dashboard/qa_lifecycle_probe/publish → 200, then GET returns { type, name, item } with the widget intact

acceptance.clause: a pending second draft does not perturb the live revision until published
acceptance.verify: after staging draft 2, GET still returns revision 1's body; after publishing draft 2, GET returns revision 2

acceptance.clause: optimistic concurrency holds: a write carrying a stale If-Match version answers 409 metadata_conflict — a concurrent edit is reported, never silently overwritten
acceptance.verify: re-PUT with the superseded version token → 409 with the metadata_conflict code (the ADR-0008 chain the receipt's version field exists for)

acceptance.clause: package-wide publish-drafts promotes every pending draft in one atomic release — and a non-compliant draft (e.g. an object draft missing the package namespace prefix) aborts the batch BEFORE any promotion
acceptance.verify: POST /api/v1/packages/<id>/publish-drafts flips both staged drafts; the namespace-gate rejection path leaves ALL drafts unpromoted (packages/objectql/src/protocol-publish-package-drafts.test.ts pins the atomicity). ⚠ SCORE THE ABORT OFF THE BODY, NOT THE STATUS (run #7695): the namespace-gate abort answers HTTP 200 with data.success:false, so a status-only assertion reads an aborted publish as a successful one. Read data.success and then prove the atomicity — the run verified the abort leaves BOTH names 404. Whether 200+success:false or a 4xx is the intended contract for this door is an OPEN LEDGER QUESTION recorded at #7753 item 2, awaiting one deliberate ruling; until it is ruled, assert the CURRENT behaviour and do not file the status code as a defect
acceptance.evidence: the publish-drafts response (status AND body) + post-state reads showing both names still 404

acceptance.clause: an invalid draft cannot cross into active: the author-time rules gate the draft→active transition (#4463) — publish of the stray-key draft is refused
acceptance.verify: the publish attempt on the invalid draft errors; the live read still serves nothing (or the prior good revision). A stray widget key is now refused already at the DRAFT save — 422 INVALID_METADATA at widgets.N, unrecognized_keys (QA run #26715) — so no invalid draft exists to publish: that refusal plus the unchanged live read scores this clause too, since nothing invalid crossed into active

acceptance.clause: Studio chrome tells the truth: the item header's 'Draft · N unpublished' line and the numbered pill on the Changes button while pending, cleared after publish
acceptance.verify: for a draft staged in a writable package (an env-wide draft is counted in no package scope, so it shows no pill): the draft line and the pill visible pre-publish, both gone post-publish and after a reload. A publish made outside Studio (the REST publish of steps[3]) shows in Studio only after a reload; Studio's own 'Publish all' clears them at once (QA run #24604) (the audit found this model 'reads consistently everywhere')

acceptance.clause: the durable history lists BOTH published revisions after two publishes — GET /meta/dashboard/qa_lifecycle_probe/history returns the sys_metadata_history events for revision 1 and revision 2 (real events because a dashboard is an overlay type; a non-overlay type returning { events: [] } is by design, not a miss)
acceptance.verify: the /history body carries the two PUBLISH events with ascending seq/version, among the draft-save events history also records (v1 draft, v2 publish, v3 draft, v4 publish on a clean two-round run) — consulted on the REST route-manager server, not the dispatcher

acceptance.clause: diff names the changed top-level key, not a whole-body dump — GET .../diff between the two PUBLISH versions read off /history (v2 → v4 on a clean run) reports `widgets` under changed[] with its before and after values, and no top-level key whose value did not change
acceptance.verify: changed[] carries an entry with path 'widgets' (the top-level key the second revision edited) whose from/to carry the two arrays, and no entry for a top-level key whose value is the same in both revisions; the diff is shallow by contract (protocol.ts#diffShallow), so a path inside the array (widgets[0].title) is NOT expected and its absence is not a FAIL, while an unchanged key listed, or the whole document under one path, is. A diff of a draft save against its own publish (from=1&to=2) reports changed [] and scores nothing either way

items.title: An invalid authored shape is rejected at save with a LOCATED error and is not persisted

requires: scratch metadata names only (qa_invalid_probe / qa_invalid_views) — rejected drafts must leave nothing behind, so no cleanup dependency

knownGaps: KNOWN SPURIOUS BANNER — do not file it as new (run #7695's sighting recorded here so it is not re-filed a third time): a freshly saved VALID draft can show "Unrecognized key(s) on this object: `_diagnostics`". The designer re-validates the server's OWN annotation on read-back — `_diagnostics` is added by the server to the saved body, and the strict client-side schema then rejects it. It is a false positive on a save that succeeded, and it is the exact inverse of what this item asserts (a LOCATED error on an INVALID shape), so it is worth telling apart on sight: if the banner names `_diagnostics` and the save returned 2xx, it is this known issue, not a validation failure

steps: attempt PUT /api/v1/meta/object/qa_invalid_probe?mode=draft with a field MISSING its type; capture the status and full error body

attempt PUT /api/v1/meta/view/qa_invalid_views?mode=draft with `type`/`columns` at the CONTAINER level (the flat-list-view mistake) BESIDE a container key (e.g. `list: {…}`), so the body is container-shaped and the container's guidance answers; capture the guidance error. Bind the body's `object` to an object that holds NO stored view container (a fresh scratch object): against one that already has a container, the container name-collision check answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR naming the other owner first and masks the guidance (protocol.ts viewContainerNameCollisionRefusal; QA run #26715 met it). A body of `type`/`columns` alone is judged as an inline view config instead and refused as naming no `object`/`viewKind` — the same 'Wrap it: defineView({ list: … })' remedy, different first sentence (packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts INLINE_VIEW_OBJECT_REQUIRED / INLINE_VIEW_KIND_REQUIRED)
after each rejection, GET the name back and record what the store holds

drive one invalid shape through the browser door that reaches the server gate — the Setup metadata editor's Source tab (/_console/apps/setup/metadata/object/NAME), whose autosave PUTs it — and capture the surfaced error. The Studio designer holds an incomplete shape client-side and never sends it ('Not saved yet: …'), so it does not exercise the 422 — it must locate the offending field, not say a generic 'save failed'
author the CORRECTED shapes (field with a type; views wrapped under list:) and confirm both save 200 — the gate rejects the shape, not the name

knownGaps: CORRECTION TO RUN #7637 (recorded by run #7695): the Studio read-only badge is HONEST on this build/pin — it is not asserting a lock the server declines to apply. With OS_METADATA_WRITABLE=permission set, GET /meta reports permission { allowEnvironmentOverlay: true, overrideSource: 'env' } (the enum is registry|env — packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts) and the editor becomes fully writable; the badge tracks the real writable computation, proven BOTH ways in that run. #7637's contrary observation does not reproduce here — do not act on it as written, and do not re-file it

ROUTE NOTE (run #7695 / #7690): a flow authored over the metadata API is NOT editable in Studio — it opens behind 'This flow is provided by an installed package, so it is read-only at runtime', with or without `?package=`. objectui's ResourceEditPage treats an item as artifact-backed when `layered.code != null && _packageId !== 'sys_metadata'` (packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ResourceEditPage.tsx / 1311-1323) and `flow` declares allowEnvironmentOverlay:false, so for THIS kind the banner is arguably telling the truth: the server would refuse the overlay write anyway. The editable path is the console's own create page. Recorded as a route note, NOT a defect — the polarity-reversed case (the same heuristic locking an object published into a WRITABLE package, which Studio and the server both treat as editable) IS the defect and is filed at objectui#4308; whoever works that card should confirm this case stays correct

steps: read the authority first: DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY in packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts declares per-kind allowEnvironmentOverlay and allowRuntimeCreate — if the flags have changed, revise this item's variants before running

cleanup + reset semantics: DELETE /api/v1/meta/view/<overlaid name> and confirm reset:true, then GET returns the artifact default again
run every probe against the LIVE server os dev runs — never a simulated dispatch

steps: ground the engine truth FIRST (rule 6 parity): for each probe expression, capture the canonical verdict from the engine — via MCP validate_expression (site: formula / flow_condition) or `objectstack build` — so the editor is judged against server truth. validate_expression has NO RLS site (formula | validation | flow_condition | template), so the RLS probes' engine verdict is the author-time gate `os build` and publish run: packages/lint/src/validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.ts (rls-predicate-unenforceable / rls-predicate-unparseable, both error tier). The ENGINE itself is pinned by ai.mcp-validate-expression / api-backend.formula-gates; this item only checks the EDITOR agrees

F1 formula result-type: open the object field designer (ObjectFieldInspector) on a formula field (type=formula, role=value, scope=record), TYPE a proven-number expression (record.est_hours * 1.1, or record.quantity * record.unit_price) and, separately, one cel-js cannot prove (record.a + record.b); after the 250ms debounce, screenshot the inferred-result-type (Σ) affordance for each

type an unknown field (record.est_hourz) and a bare field ref in record scope (est_hours, no record. prefix); capture the inline error under the field (aria-invalid, destructive border) and its record.<field> fix text

F2 conditional-rule editor: open the same field's visibleWhen editor (scope=record, roots record/previous/parent); type `previous.` and then `record.` and capture the autocomplete listbox — it must offer the object's field catalog; type `current_user.` and confirm it does NOT list this object's fields; accept a suggestion and confirm the insertion

F4 RLS editor: in Studio open /_console/studio/PKG/access, select the permission set, open its 'Row-level security' tab (PermissionAdvancedFacets) and add a policy on the object; enter a USING predicate that is NOT a simple field comparison (blast-radius), one with a parse fault, and — the virtual-field probe — one comparing the object's FORMULA field (e.g. record.FORMULA_FIELD > 5: a formula field has no storage column, so the engine cannot push the filter down and refuses it, rls-predicate-unenforceable, packages/lint/src/validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.ts#RLS_PREDICATE_UNENFORCEABLE); confirm ALL THREE raise a blocking ERROR: the non-pushdownable filter at the engine's tier — rls-predicate-unenforceable refuses it at build and publish (ADR-0056 D4) because the runtime drops the policy and fails CLOSED, so it grants no access — and the parse fault as a parse error; with an error present the save is held (celErrorCount>0): the environment door's Save is disabled with title perm.cel.saveBlocked, and the Studio package door, which autosaves and has no Save button, shows the perm-autosave-held status and issues no PUT

acceptance.verify: after a screenshot confirms the editor rendered, the autocomplete listbox after 'previous.' / 'record.' lists field names; after 'current_user.' it does not list this object's fields; a bare 'est_hours' shows the record.<field> error

acceptance.clause: the RLS lint and the save gate agree with the engine: a non-pushdownable USING read filter raises a blocking ERROR, not an advisory warning, because the engine refuses it (rls-predicate-unenforceable, ADR-0056 D4) and the runtime fails CLOSED — the policy is dropped and grants no access, it never widens access — and a parse fault raises a blocking ERROR too; with either error present the save is held (celErrorCount>0) — a predicate the engine refuses cannot be persisted

items.title: Permission-matrix editor UX: field-filter + bulk apply to EXACTLY the visible fields, and the Bulk column never clips at narrow widths

requires: a writable permission set to edit in the Permission Matrix editor (env-scope metadata-admin, or a package permission set in the Studio Access pillar) — a read-only source-loaded set can be opened to verify the read-only gate but not to exercise bulk writes

an object with MORE THAN 6 fields to expand in the matrix, so the field sub-table's filter renders (FieldsSubTable shows the filter only when fields.length > 6) — a stock showcase object with a wide field set (showcase_account / showcase_invoice) on the environment door, or an object OF THE PACKAGE in the Studio Access pillar: in package scope the matrix lists only the package's own objects (objectui PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx, 'In package scope, list only the objects this package declares'), so a scratch package's set reads '0 objects granted' even when it grants showcase_account (QA run #24604)
a narrow viewport for the Bulk-column clip check (B3)

in package scope, the package's objects PUBLISHED before the set is opened: while they are only drafts, the Studio Access matrix lists none of them ('0 objects') — a defect QA run #26715 recorded (the matrix lists objects without the draft preview); publish them first, or record the leg blocked(fixture) citing the run

A jsdom unit pin runs here (`pnpm --filter @object-ui/PKG exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 FILE`); a ui/e2e/live spec runs from ui/ with `pnpm test:e2e:live SPEC` against a live backend and the console dev server (the prerequisites are in ui/playwright.live.config.ts). steps: open the Permission Matrix editor on a writable permission set (Studio Access pillar, /_console/studio/PKG/access, or the metadata admin's door /_console/apps/com.objectstack.setup/metadata/permission/<name>; ⛔ not /_console/apps/com.objectstack.studio/…, the studio app is not loaded on a stock boot — RUNNER.md environment facts); expand an object with > 6 fields so the field sub-table's filter renders (threshold is > 6)

B4 field filter: type a filter that narrows the field set to a couple of fields; confirm the sub-table's 'n / N' counter and the DOM show only the matching fields (the hidden fields' read/edit checkboxes are absent)

B4 bulk-over-visible: click 'Write all' (perm.field.bulk.writable) → it must grant read+write to EXACTLY the visible fields; clear the filter and confirm the previously-hidden fields are UNTOUCHED (still at their prior grant), never bulk-applied

on a different filtered set click 'Read-only all' (perm.field.bulk.readable) → it revokes write on the visible fields only; click 'Clear' → it drops the explicit overrides so the visible fields fall back to the read-only default (readable, not editable)

Save; GET /api/v1/meta/permission/<name> (or the package draft read) and assert the fields map (keyed `${object}.${field}`) carries overrides for ONLY the fields that were visible when each bulk fired — never a filter-hidden field

B3 clip: shrink the viewport to a narrow width; confirm the object matrix's enclosing overflow-auto container SCROLLS horizontally (the table carries min-w-[1304px]; Studio's is data-testid perm-studio-matrix) and the Bulk column (Read / CRUD / All / None per row) stays reachable, not clipped off the right edge

read-only gate: open a read-only package/type set; confirm Save is hidden, every checkbox is disabled, the field sub-table's bulk buttons (Read-only all / Write all / Clear) are ABSENT — FieldsSubTable renders them only while the set is writable — and the object row's Read / CRUD / All / None, which Studio shows only on the row under the pointer or with keyboard focus, are disabled when they show; the read-only badge names package-vs-type as the reason

the grant→access flip (a flipped verb actually changing a persona's API access) is access-security.permission-matrix-edit-loop — cite a pass there; this item does NOT re-prove that a saved grant changes access

acceptance.clause: the field filter narrows the sub-table to the matching fields only — the visible/total counter and the DOM both reflect the filtered set (hidden fields' read/edit checkboxes absent)
acceptance.verify: after a screenshot confirms the sub-table rendered, only the filtered field rows are present and the 'n / N' counter matches the filtered count
acceptance.evidence: the filtered sub-table DOM read + screenshot

acceptance.clause: a field bulk (Write all / Read-only all) applies to EXACTLY the visible/filtered fields — after the bulk, clearing the filter shows the previously-hidden fields still at their prior grant, so the wrong-scope write never happened (objectui#2600 B4)
acceptance.verify: filter → bulk → clear filter: the hidden fields' read/edit checkbox states are unchanged from before the bulk
acceptance.evidence: before/after checkbox states across the filter clear

acceptance.clause: server truth proves the scope: the SAVED permission set's fields map (keyed `${object}.${field}`) carries overrides for ONLY the fields visible at bulk time — a filter-hidden field must not appear from a bulk it was never part of
acceptance.verify: GET /meta/permission/<name>: the fields-map keys touched by a bulk are a subset of the field names visible when that bulk fired

acceptance.clause: 'Clear' drops the explicit overrides for the visible fields so they fall back to the default (readable, not editable) — the saved fields map no longer carries those keys, rather than writing an explicit default row
acceptance.verify: after Clear + Save, the cleared fields' keys are absent from the fields map

acceptance.clause: at a narrow viewport the object matrix container scrolls horizontally and the Bulk column (Read / CRUD / All / None) stays reachable — the min-w-[1304px] table forces a scrollbar instead of clipping the last column off the right edge (objectui#2600 B3)
acceptance.verify: at a narrow width the matrix container's scrollWidth exceeds its clientWidth and, after a horizontal scroll (scrollLeft > 0), a screenshot shows the full Bulk column. A painted scrollbar is not required: headless Chromium uses overlay scrollbars that paint none (QA run #24604) — the scroll is the evidence
acceptance.evidence: the narrow-viewport screenshot(s) before and after the scroll + the scrollWidth / clientWidth reading

acceptance.clause: the read-only gate holds: a read-only set hides Save, offers no field bulk at all and no operating object-row bulk, and disables every checkbox; the read-only badge names WHICH gate holds
acceptance.verify: on the read-only set Save is absent, every checkbox is disabled, the field bulk buttons (Read-only all / Write all / Clear) are absent — not merely disabled (PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx FieldsSubTable renders them only while writable; QA run #26715 read them absent in read-only Studio) — and the object row's bulk, which appears only on hover or keyboard focus (engine.studio.access.bulkHint), is disabled when it appears; an operating bulk control is the FAIL. The badge names the gate that holds; the console distinguishes FOUR (objectui PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx at the pin): the package gate (engine.studio.pkg.readonly — Studio on a read-only package), the artifact gate (perm.readOnly.artifact, 'Read-only (this set is provided by a code package)' — a set a code package ships, in the metadata admin), the wall (perm.readOnly.walled — the security catalog under isolated/group tenancy) and the type gate (perm.readOnly — a type with no runtime write channel). On a stock boot only the package and artifact gates are reachable — the wall needs a walled tenancy posture and the type gate a permission type with no write channel, which stock does not have — so score those two on the packaged showcase_contributor set (Studio Access and the metadata admin) and record the other two as not reachable on stock. A badge that blames the wrong gate is the FAIL

negative: a field bulk that writes grants to fields hidden by the filter is the FAIL this item exists for — a wrong bulk scope silently grants or revokes access on fields the admin never saw (assert against the SAVED fields map, not the repaint)
the Bulk column clipped off the right edge at a narrow width with no horizontal scroll is the B3 FAIL — the admin cannot reach Read / CRUD / All / None
variants: field bulk: Read-only all (readable)
field bulk: Write all (writable)
field bulk: Clear

items.title: Source-authored page tiers render by the RIGHT path: kind:'html' source is PARSED-never-executed (static, in-browser sdui-parser compile), kind:'react' source is EXECUTED behind its capability gate (live data + interactivity) — command-center-jsx / capability-map (html) vs crm-workbench (react)
personas: admin (seeded admin@objectos.ai) driving the published showcase app as an end user

requires: seeded showcase_project rows (the react page's live KPI + <ListView> read them)

the react-pages capability ON — CAP_REACT_PAGES defaults OFF and the showcase turns it on in its committed .env (OS_PAGE_REACT_ENABLED=true); a boot with OS_PAGE_REACT_ENABLED=false flips it OFF (the both-sides gate check)
knownGaps: NO manual build step is needed to VIEW either tier in the running showcase (contra the task's guess): a kind:'html' page compiles IN-BROWSER via @object-ui/sdui-parser compile(source, manifest) at render, against a whitelist manifest built from the LIVE ComponentRegistry (packages/components/src/renderers/layout/page.tsx); a kind:'react' page is transpiled IN-BROWSER by a lazily-loaded Sucrase @object-ui/react-runtime chunk. The only build-shaped risk is the vendored /_console bundle being stale (stale-console-bundle) — a stale sdui-parser/react-runtime mis-compiles a page that is fine on a fresh build. ⚠ A FAULTING html source never reaches the RENDERED page on a stock boot: the metadata save door compiles an html page's source against the deployment's manifest with the same compiler `os validate` uses (packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts#HTML_PAGE_SOURCE_COMPILE), so an active save or a publish of a faulting html page answers 422 INVALID_METADATA carrying the compile diagnostics, and nothing is served. The 'HTML page failed to compile (N)' panel is therefore reachable only in the page designer's DRAFT preview, where a ?mode=draft save of the faulting source is admitted and rendered (QA run #23166)

acceptance.evidence: the click's network capture (no request) + the disabled switch's DOM state and its accessible description

acceptance.clause: inspector edits are inert OR their discard is announced: the flow node inspector on a read-only package either disables its inputs or tells the author the edit will not persist — an edit that visibly takes and silently vanishes on reload is the failure

items.title: The metadata governance sweep: GET /meta/diagnostics reports every STORED item failing spec validation with located errors, refuses outages and bad spellings loudly instead of answering '0 problems', and the Studio diagnostics page + directory tile badges paint the same numbers

requires: a console built from this tree with `pnpm console:build` (the DiagnosticsPage / DirectoryPage halves are objectui code under ui/)
the stock metadata corpus (any booted showcase — the sweep runs over whatever the store holds)
knownGaps: THE POSITIVE ENTRY LEG NEEDS A PLANTED ROW, AND ONE CAN BE PLANTED ON THE RUN'S OWN SCRATCH FILE DB (QA run #24604): every authoring door validates at save (the 422 gate studio-authoring.authoring-validation-not-persisted proves), so a stock store holds NO invalid item and the sweep legitimately answers clean — entries:[], total:0 — and sys_metadata is a storage table, not a data-plane object, so /api/v1/data cannot plant one. The recipe: save a VALID view through the door WITH ?package=<a writable package> (DirectoryPage is always package-scoped, so a package-less row never reaches a tile badge), then rewrite that row's sys_metadata.metadata in the scratch SQLite file (e.g. config.columns[0].field = 123); the next sweep reports it with no restart, and deleting the row restores a clean sweep. ⛔ Only on the run's own file DB, never a shared one. The located-error half is also unit-pinned at the producer: packages/metadata-protocol/src/metadata-diagnostics.union-issues.test.ts (computeMetadataDiagnostics names the offending key per union branch, and decorateMetadataItem carries it). That pin scores neither the sweep entry nor the page's deep link

severity=warning ADDS NO ROWS ON TODAY'S PRODUCERS: the sweep's contract includes warning-only entries (protocol.ts getMetaDiagnostics: valid items with diagnostics.warnings), but computeMetadataDiagnostics emits errors only and the docstring reserves warnings 'for a future lint layer' — no read-decoration producer emits a warning at head. The severity clause asserts the MECHANISM (param accepted, error rows unchanged), not warning rows; a warning row appearing is a finding that the lint layer landed (revise this item), never noise

REPO OWNERSHIP (ADR-0054): the API half — route, sweep, stats, refusals — is objectstack's; the page markup, grouping, deep links, badges are objectui's (metadata-admin/DiagnosticsPage.tsx, DirectoryPage.tsx, useMetadata.ts). A locator or copy fix goes to objectui

steps: boot the showcase on its own port and DB (dogfood §0); sign in as the dev admin

GET /api/v1/meta/diagnostics on the live REST server and record the BARE body — { entries, total, scannedTypes, scannedItems, stats } with NO { success, data } envelope on this surface (rest-route-ledger.ts); ⛔ the route is REST-server-only, so a simulated dispatch is not an oracle here

stats parity probe: for two or three types (object, view, flow), GET /api/v1/meta/<type> and compare stats[<type>].count against the list's item count and stats[<type>].packages against the sorted distinct _packageId set of those items

package scoping: GET /api/v1/meta/diagnostics?package=com.example.showcase and record how stats narrows; then open Studio's metadata directory (/apps/<app>/metadata?package=com.example.showcase) and compare the tile counts against the scoped stats (DirectoryPage feeds its tiles from the package-scoped sweep)
severity mechanism: GET /api/v1/meta/diagnostics?severity=warning — capture that it answers 200 and that the error entries are unchanged (no warning producer exists at head; see knownGaps)

refusal probes: GET /api/v1/meta/diagnostics?type=viewes (an unrecognised spelling of a DECLARED type) and capture the 400; GET /api/v1/meta/diagnostics?severity=error&severity=warning (a repeated query param) and capture that refusal too

browser, clean store: open /apps/<app>/metadata/_diagnostics — screenshot it settled; on a clean corpus the DESIGNED empty state must render (title + the scanned-items/types counts), never a blank region; back on the directory page confirm the red diagnostics-link button is ABSENT (it renders only when total > 0). The directory always repairs ?package= to a project package, so the button is judged per package scope
outage clause: run the unit pin (packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.diagnostics-store-outage.test.ts) and cite its output — driving a live store outage is not attempted

invalid-row leg (plant the row first, fixtures.knownGaps[0]): re-GET the sweep — the planted row must appear as { type, name, diagnostics: { errors: [{ path, message }] } } with the LOCATED path, the page must group it under its type with a deep link to ../<type>/<name> (the item's editor), and the directory badge count must include it

acceptance.clause: the sweep contract holds on the live server: the bare body carries entries/total/scannedTypes/scannedItems/stats, total === entries.length, and scannedTypes covers exactly the registry types with a registered Zod schema (schema-less types are skipped as 'no opinion' — never counted valid, never failing the sweep)
acceptance.verify: the recorded body parses against GetMetaDiagnosticsResponseSchema's shape (protocol.zod.ts); total equals the entries length; scannedTypes is the registry-with-schema count, not the full registry count (getMetaDiagnostics filters on getMetadataTypeSchema)

acceptance.clause: stats tell the directory's truth: per sampled type, stats[type].count equals the type's own list length and stats[type].packages equals the sorted distinct _packageId set — the one-round-trip aggregate the Studio directory tiles render from
acceptance.verify: side-by-side of stats[<type>] against the GET /meta/<type> list for each sampled type (count, packages). `locked` counts the items whose served READ ENVELOPE reports a lock other than 'none' — the derivation the LAYERED read publishes — read it from GET /api/v1/meta/<type>/<name>/layers, whose envelope carries `lock` (protocol.ts servedLockState, #21694); the default GET /api/v1/meta/<type>/<name> is the cached arm and carries no `lock` by design, so it cannot answer this — NOT the rows whose declared `_lock` != 'none': a packaged base the write doors refuse reads locked on its envelope while declaring no `_lock`, so compare `locked` against each sampled item's envelope lock
acceptance.evidence: the stats excerpt + the list reads

acceptance.clause: ?package= scoping narrows the whole sweep and the Studio directory tiles match it: with the sweep scoped to com.example.showcase, stats reflect only that package's items, and the rendered tile counts on the package-scoped directory equal the scoped stats — tile numbers match the scoped list pages, not the global corpus
acceptance.verify: the ?package= body's stats vs the unscoped body; then the directory tiles (rendered only after the screenshot confirms the page settled) vs stats[<type>].count — DirectoryPage drives them from useGlobalDiagnostics(client, 'warning', activePackage), so a mismatch is a real seam defect
acceptance.evidence: scoped + unscoped stats, and the tile screenshot annotated with the compared counts

acceptance.clause: an unrecognised spelling of a declared type is REFUSED, never absorbed: ?type=viewes answers the 400 INVALID_REQUEST that names both accepted spellings — not 200 {"scannedTypes":1,"stats":{}}, which objectui's page paints as 'All clear' (#8924: the producer classified the caller's mistake; the sweep may not overrule a verdict into silence)
acceptance.verify: the ?type=viewes response is 400 with the canonicalizeMetaRequestType refusal (the same one every sibling /meta door gives); the ?severity=error&severity=warning probe is refused too (refuseRepeatedQueryParams, #6877 — severity/type/package are all single-valued)

acceptance.clause: severity=warning is accepted and widens only by contract: the response is 200, the error entries are byte-identical to the severity=error sweep, and no warning rows appear — because no producer emits warnings at head ('reserved for a future lint layer'); the clause records that posture so a future warning row is recognised as the lint layer landing, not a defect
acceptance.verify: diff the two sweeps' entries; identical at head. A NEW warning-only entry appearing is not a FAIL — it is the trigger to revise this item (and the UI already wires it: warn-only rows get the amber badge, error rows dominate)

acceptance.clause: the clean store renders the DESIGNED empty state, and absence is honest in both directions: the DiagnosticsPage shows its all-clear title with the scanned counts (never a blank region), and the directory's red diagnostics-link button does not render while total is 0
acceptance.verify: the settled /metadata/_diagnostics screenshot shows the Empty state with the scannedItems/scannedTypes numbers matching the API body; the directory header has no diagnostics button (DirectoryPage renders it only when diagSummary.total > 0)
acceptance.evidence: the two screenshots + the API body's counts

acceptance.clause: an invalid STORED item surfaces with a located error and a working deep link: the sweep lists it as type+name+errors[{path,message}] (union failures named per-branch via zodIssuesToMetadataIssues — never one rootless 'Invalid input', #5598), the page groups it under its type, and the row's link lands on that item's editor — on a row planted on the run's own scratch file DB (knownGaps[0]); the save gates keep stock clean
acceptance.verify: with the planted row: the entry's diagnostics.errors carry the failing path (rootless union-parent entries — path '' or config.columns, 'Invalid input' — may ride beside the located leaf; the clause needs the located leaf present, not their absence); clicking the row navigates to ../<type>/<name> (the ResourceEditPage for the item); the DirectoryPage invalid badge for that type increments to match
acceptance.evidence: the sweep entry + the deep-link navigation screenshot

acceptance.clause: a store outage is a loud 503, never '0 problems': when the metadata store read fails for a non-benign reason, getMetaDiagnostics rethrows the classified 503 instead of publishing an unreadable store as a clean sweep (#8855; ADR-0110 D3 — a miss and an outage are different facts)
acceptance.verify: run packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.diagnostics-store-outage.test.ts and cite its output — the pin drives the outage this item does not stage live

negative: a 200 {"scannedTypes":1,"stats":{}} for a misspelled declared type is the #8924 silence regressed — the page would paint it 'All clear' — FAIL

an outage answered as a clean sweep (total 0 from a store nobody could read) is the #8855 / ADR-0110 D3 FAIL shape — a diagnostics endpoint whose job is reporting problems must not answer '0 problems' precisely when it cannot read anything

a blank diagnostics region on a clean store (instead of the designed empty state) is a FAIL of the page, not proof of health — and conversely, do NOT read the clean answer itself as 'the feature is missing': a store with no invalid rows is the healthy norm the save gates enforce (absence-inference)

consulting the dispatcher for this route is a recording error — the ledger marks GET /meta/diagnostics REST-server-only, so a simulated dispatch 404 says nothing about the live server (dispatcher-vs-hono-route)

SCOPE: per-item _diagnostics badges on list rows and the editor banner are the item-grain surfaces (ResourceListPage/ResourceEditPage) — this item owns only the cross-type sweep + directory/diagnostics pages; the save-time 422 gate is studio-authoring.authoring-validation-not-persisted — cite, don't duplicate

items.title: A doc on the app menu follows the reader's audience: an admin authors a doc and puts it (or its book) on an app menu; a member who may read it sees it and opens it in its book; a member outside its audience does not see the entry and gets a refusal — never "not found", never a blank page — on the direct route
personas: seeded admin (authors the doc, the books and the app navigation)
member holding the gating permission set (the reader)

requires: a book with audience { permissionSet: SET } claiming one doc, an org book claiming another, and a book claiming none — all in ONE package, so the flat /docs/DOC permalink has to pick the CLAIMING book rather than the package's first book by label
an app whose navigation carries one doc entry of each shape — { doc }, { book }, { book, doc } — over the gated and the open corpus

a session per persona, each signed in through the form in its own browser context; the member holding SET gets it through a sys_user_permission_set row (a stock set such as showcase_auditor serves as SET)
a console bundle carrying objectui PR 11258 (menu pruning, direct-route refusal, claiming-book permalink) and PR 11241 (the doc editor)
knownGaps: THE STOCK SHOWCASE CORPUS CARRIES NO { permissionSet } BOOK AND NO doc NAV ENTRY — verify first (GET /api/v1/meta/book, read each audience; GET /api/v1/meta/app?id=showcase_app, look for type:'doc'). The run authors the books, docs, permission set and nav entries at runtime and tears them down, as platform-core.docs-audience-gate allows; the audience is read off the stored row, so a runtime-authored book exercises the same resolver

FORK WINDOW CLOSED: every objectui revision from daeb77fc84dd on carried objectui PR 11241 and PR 11258, and so does the objectui code imported under ui/ — the 'You do not have access to this documentation' refusal page and the menu pruning — so a console built from this tree with `pnpm console:build` is the right one to drive (QA run #23942 ran outside the window). Only a console older than those PRs (db11afd496 held neither, source read) fails for a reason that is not this item's; record the commit the console was built from in the run record as usual

FIXTURE RECIPE, measured on the first run: the showcase is invite_only, so members come from POST /api/v1/auth/admin/create-user, not sign-up — and the body must SEND `mustChangePassword: false`: the door defaults it to true (packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-user-endpoints.ts#runAdminCreateUser), and a member left on true cannot drive the menu until it has changed its password (QA run #26715); the Studio doc editor no longer refuses the read-only code package with a 422 — at objectui 1fb1ced36243 it saves an ENV-WIDE draft and offers no package picker (QA run #23166), so a doc authored through the editor lands outside the package that holds the books. Install a writable base first (POST /api/v1/packages with id, name, version, type 'app') and drive every book, doc and the app into it over the metadata API with ?package=, so books and docs share one package; the seeded admin holds no app-declared set, so once the gated book claims the doc the admin's own editor and /meta/app answer the audience refusal too — author the doc before the gated book, or read it back as the reader

items.title: A removed metadata key is refused at the save door at its real location, with a prescription, and nothing is stored — for the 33 keys QA run #26715 drove across nine types — whether the key still carries its tombstone or its retirement kit has aged out

requires: a fresh boot of the showcase on its own port and DB (dogfood §0) with OS_PORT exported, signed in as the seeded admin

a writable package (the save door judges a ?package= draft as Studio writes it) and a clean baseline draft of each type — object, hook, action, view, app, page, dashboard, flow, permission — that saves 200 BEFORE any removed key is added, so a refusal is the key's and not the body's
knownGaps: TWO REFUSAL SHAPES AT HEAD, BOTH CORRECT (read at 43731031). QA run #26715, at 3fcafcd3, saw all 33 refused with the per-key sentence '… was removed in @objectstack/spec N … use … / delete …'. Since #26599 the retirement kits that retired at or below 16.x have aged out: 22 of the 33 keys no longer carry a tombstone and are refused as an ordinary unknown key, whose message names the nearest declared spelling and ends with the protocol-upgrade-guide sentence (packages/spec/src/shared/protocol-upgrade-guide.ts#RETIRED_KEY_UPGRADE_GUIDE_SENTENCE). variants mark which shape each key answers at HEAD; a key moving from one shape to the other is not a fail

steps: for each type, PUT the clean baseline draft (?mode=draft&package=PKG) and confirm 200
for each variant row, PUT the baseline with the removed key added at the location the row names; capture status, code, the issue path and the message
after each refusal GET the draft (?state=draft&package=PKG) and confirm it is still the baseline
junk-key control: PUT the view baseline with a top-level key zzz_junk_key: true, then the object, page and dashboard baselines with the same key; read each stored draft

acceptance.clause: every removed key is refused 422 INVALID_METADATA at its real location, with a prescription: where the key still carries its tombstone, an issue at the key's own path whose message is that key's retirement sentence; where its kit aged out, the unknown-key refusal at the PARENT object's path, naming the key, with the protocol upgrade guide sentence
acceptance.verify: per row: status 422, code INVALID_METADATA, and one of the two shapes, never a bare unrecognized-key line with no way forward. Tombstone: an issue whose path is the key's location and whose message is its retiredKey sentence, either 'was removed in @objectstack/spec …' for a removed key or 'was renamed to `NEW` in @objectstack/spec … Rename the key …' for a rename tombstone such as dashboard.refreshInterval (→ refreshIntervalSeconds, packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.zod.ts). Aged out: an unrecognized_keys issue whose path is the PARENT object that holds the key (unknown keys are reported on their container), whose message names the key ('Unrecognized key(s) on SURFACE: `KEY`.') and carries the upgrade-guide sentence (packages/spec/src/shared/suggestions.zod.ts, RETIRED_KEY_UPGRADE_GUIDE_SENTENCE)
acceptance.evidence: one line per key: status, code, path, the message's prescription half

acceptance.clause: nothing is stored: each refused save leaves the baseline draft unchanged
acceptance.verify: the draft read after each refusal equals the baseline

acceptance.clause: an unknown top-level key is refused on every type's envelope alike — the view envelope included — never answered 200 and dropped
acceptance.verify: the junk-key PUT answers 422 unrecognized_keys for view as for object, page and dashboard, and no stored draft lacks a key the author sent while the save answered 200
acceptance.evidence: the four answers + the stored drafts

negative: a 200 for a removed key — stored, or silently stripped — is the FAIL: the author (or an AI) reads success while the key is discarded

SCOPE: retired keys at parse and build (query and error-envelope tombstones, the retired filter operators) are api-backend.enforce-or-remove-authoring-gates; the save door's authoring LINT rules are studio-authoring.save-door-runs-authoring-rules

items.title: A write that names a package nobody installed is refused, for every metadata type as it already is for flows: the save door answers WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED and stores nothing, publish-drafts on that id promotes nothing, and Studio opened on it says the package does not exist instead of rendering a writable builder

requires: a fresh boot of the showcase on its own port and DB (dogfood §0) with OS_PORT exported, signed in as the seeded admin, and a console built from this tree with `pnpm console:build`
a package id that no package carries, e.g. com.example.nosuch — confirm GET /api/v1/packages/com.example.nosuch answers 404 first

steps: control: PUT /api/v1/meta/flow/qa_ghost_flow?mode=draft&package=com.example.nosuch with a valid flow body; capture status, code and message

the same named-package save for an object (a valid body with sharingModel), a dashboard and a page, each once with ?mode=draft and once as an active save; capture each answer, then GET each name with ?state=draft&package=com.example.nosuch and without
POST /api/v1/packages/com.example.nosuch/publish-drafts; capture the answer; GET the names live
GET /api/v1/meta/diagnostics and read stats.<type>.packages for the phantom id
open /_console/studio/com.example.nosuch and /_console/studio/com.example.nosuch/data; screenshot each settled; then open /_console/studio/<a real writable package>/bogus_pillar
teardown: DELETE every name the run stored (DELETE /api/v1/meta/TYPE/NAME?package=com.example.nosuch, and ?state=draft for drafts) and re-read until each answers 404

acceptance.clause: control: a flow saved into an uninstalled package is refused 422 WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED, naming the package, and nothing is written
acceptance.verify: status 422, code WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED, the message names com.example.nosuch and says nothing was written; the read-back answers 404

acceptance.clause: object, dashboard and page saves naming the uninstalled package are refused the same way — draft and active alike — and nothing is stored
acceptance.verify: each save answers 4xx (WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED, as for flow) and each read-back answers 404
acceptance.evidence: one line per save + its read-back

acceptance.clause: publish-drafts on an uninstalled package id promotes nothing, and no phantom package appears in the diagnostics stats
acceptance.verify: the publish answers 404 (or a refusal) and every name stays 404 live; stats.<type>.packages lists no com.example.nosuch
acceptance.evidence: the publish answer + the live reads + the stats excerpt

acceptance.clause: Studio opened on a package that does not exist shows that it does not exist, with a way back — never a writable builder; an unknown pillar segment does not silently render another pillar
acceptance.verify: the not-found state for both URLs (no New object, no Create app); the bogus pillar URL is not shown as the Interfaces pillar with the bogus URL kept

negative: a 200 for a write bound to a package that does not exist is the FAIL: the row is invisible to the package doors that would govern it, and it skips the namespace gate on the way in

SCOPE: the read-only package refusals (WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED and ITEM_LOCKED on com.example.showcase) are studio-authoring.first-run-loop's negative probe and access-security.readonly-package-locks-studio; multi-package row addressing is studio-authoring.multi-package-item-rows
